Assessment 1.question: What is the fundamental theorem of arithmetic primarily concerned with?
options: The properties of rational numbers
The unique factorization of composite numbers into prime factors
The relationship between integers and fractions
The classification of real numbers into different sets
Assessment 1.answer: The unique factorization of composite numbers into prime factors

Assessment 1.question: According to the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, every composite number can be expressed as a product of what type of numbers?
options: Only even numbers
Only odd numbers
Prime numbers
Natural numbers

Assessment 1.question: Which of the following is NOT a prime number?
What is the smallest prime number?
How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 10?
What is the definition of a composite number in terms of its factors?
options: It has exactly two factors: 1 and itself
It has more than two factors
It has only one factor
It has no factors
Assessment 1.answer: It has more than two factors

Assessment 1.question: Which of the following numbers is a prime number?
What is the fundamental theorem of arithmetic also known as?
options: Prime factorization theorem
Unique factorization theorem
Euclidean division algorithm
Fundamental division principle

Assessment 1.question: Which of the following is a property of prime numbers?
options: They can be expressed as a product of two composite numbers
They have exactly two positive divisors: 1 and themselves
They are always even numbers
They cannot be divided by any number except 1
Assessment 1.answer: They have exactly two positive divisors: 1 and themselves

Assessment 1.question: What is the prime factorization of 12?
Which of the following numbers is NOT a composite number?
What does the fundamental theorem of arithmetic state about the factorization of any natural number greater than 1?
options: It can be factorized in multiple ways with different prime factors
It has a unique prime factorization except for the order of factors
It cannot be factorized into prime numbers
It must include at least one even prime number
Assessment 1.answer: It has a unique prime factorization except for the order of factors

Assessment 1.question: Which of the following represents the prime factorization of 30?
What is the prime factorization of 100?
How many distinct prime factors does the number 18 have?

Assessment 2.question: Why is the fundamental theorem of arithmetic important in mathematics?
options: It helps to determine if a number is even or odd
It provides a unique way to express any composite number as a product of primes
It allows us to find the square root of any number
It helps in determining the divisibility rules for all numbers
Assessment 2.answer: It provides a unique way to express any composite number as a product of primes

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem of arithmetic help in finding the highest common factor (HCF) of two numbers?
options: By adding the prime factors of both numbers
By taking the lowest power of all common prime factors
By multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors
By dividing one number by another
Assessment 2.answer: By taking the lowest power of all common prime factors

Assessment 2.question: Why is 1 not considered a prime number?
options: Because it has only one factor
Because it cannot be expressed as a product of primes
Because it is neither prime nor composite
Because it is an odd number
Assessment 2.answer: Because it is neither prime nor composite

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem of arithmetic help in finding the least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers?
options: By taking the highest power of all prime factors present in both numbers
By multiplying the HCF and LCM together
By dividing one number by another
By adding the prime factors of both numbers
Assessment 2.answer: By taking the highest power of all prime factors present in both numbers

Assessment 2.question: Why is the uniqueness property of prime factorization important?
options: It makes calculations faster
It ensures that every composite number has only one way to be expressed as a product of primes
It helps in identifying even and odd numbers
It allows us to write any number in decimal form
Assessment 2.answer: It ensures that every composite number has only one way to be expressed as a product of primes

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem help in determining if two numbers are coprime?
options: If they have no common factors other than 1
If they both are prime numbers
If their sum is even
If they are both divisible by 2
Assessment 2.answer: If they have no common factors other than 1

Assessment 2.question: Why do we need to express numbers in terms of prime factorization?
options: To make them look more complex
To simplify calculations involving HCF and LCM
To identify whether a number is even or odd
To find the square root of any number
Assessment 2.answer: To simplify calculations involving HCF and LCM

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem of arithmetic relate to the concept of divisibility?
options: It helps in determining if a number is divisible by another
It provides a method to find all divisors of any number
It allows us to check divisibility by 2, 3, and 5 only
It makes all numbers divisible by 1
Assessment 2.answer: It provides a method to find all divisors of any number

Assessment 2.question: Why is the fundamental theorem of arithmetic considered a foundation for number theory?
options: Because it was discovered by ancient Greek mathematicians
Because it establishes the basic structure of natural numbers in terms of primes
Because it helps in solving quadratic equations
Because it provides formulas for calculating areas
Assessment 2.answer: Because it establishes the basic structure of natural numbers in terms of primes

Assessment 2.question: How does prime factorization help in simplifying fractions?
options: By making the numerator larger
By finding common factors in numerator and denominator
By converting them to decimal form
By multiplying both numerator and denominator by 2
Assessment 2.answer: By finding common factors in numerator and denominator

Assessment 2.question: Why is it necessary to consider the order of prime factors when using the fundamental theorem?
options: Because it affects the final result
Because the theorem states that order doesn't matter
Because it makes calculations easier
Because it helps in identifying even numbers
Assessment 2.answer: Because the theorem states that order doesn't matter

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem help in proving mathematical properties?
options: By providing a method to count prime numbers
By giving a unique representation of any composite number
By helping to solve linear equations
By making it easier to find square roots
Assessment 2.answer: By giving a unique representation of any composite number

Assessment 2.question: Why is the fundamental theorem of arithmetic considered unique?
options: Because it was discovered by only one mathematician
Because every composite number has exactly one prime factorization
Because it applies to only even numbers
Because it helps in finding the average of numbers
Assessment 2.answer: Because every composite number has exactly one prime factorization

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem help in understanding the relationship between HCF and LCM?
options: By showing that HCF is always greater than LCM
By establishing that HCF × LCM = Product of two numbers
By proving that both are equal for any two numbers
By demonstrating that they are never equal
Assessment 2.answer: By establishing that HCF × LCM = Product of two numbers

Assessment 2.question: Why is it important to understand that 1 is neither prime nor composite?
options: Because it helps in identifying even numbers
Because it ensures the uniqueness of prime factorization
Because it makes calculations easier
Because it allows us to divide by any number
Assessment 2.answer: Because it ensures the uniqueness of prime factorization

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem help in solving real-world problems involving numbers?
options: By providing a method to find square roots
By helping to organize and categorize numbers systematically
By making all numbers divisible by 2
By allowing us to count prime numbers
Assessment 2.answer: By helping to organize and categorize numbers systematically

Assessment 2.question: Why is the fundamental theorem of arithmetic essential for understanding divisibility rules?
options: Because it helps in finding the sum of digits
Because it provides a systematic way to understand factors and multiples
Because it makes all numbers divisible by 3
Because it helps in identifying odd numbers
Assessment 2.answer: Because it provides a systematic way to understand factors and multiples

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem of arithmetic support the concept of unique factorization?
options: By proving that every number has exactly one prime factorization
By showing that numbers can be factorized in multiple ways
By demonstrating that all numbers are even
By establishing that 1 is a prime number
Assessment 2.answer: By proving that every number has exactly one prime factorization

Assessment 2.question: Why do we need to express composite numbers as products of primes?
options: Because it makes them look more complex
Because it provides a systematic approach for mathematical operations
Because it helps in identifying odd numbers
Because it allows us to multiply by 2
Assessment 2.answer: Because it provides a systematic approach for mathematical operations

Assessment 2.question: How does the fundamental theorem help in understanding the concept of prime numbers?
options: By showing that all numbers are prime
By establishing that every number can be expressed as a product of primes
By proving that 1 is a prime number
By demonstrating that there are no even prime numbers
Assessment 2.answer: By establishing that every number can be expressed as a product of primes
